request.statement:
Dependency-Closed Index Join Plan

A document filter refers to logical property aliases supplied by physical indexes. Names of aliases and indexes are case-insensitive ASCII identifiers; lowercase forms are canonical. Type names are case-sensitive ASCII identifiers.

The schema contains declarations `(alias, index, type)` and directed index dependencies `(from, to)`. A schema is conflicting if:

- one canonical alias is declared with different types;
- one canonical index is declared with different types; or
- either endpoint of a dependency is not an index occurring in a declaration.

Repeated declarations and dependencies are allowed. Dependency cycles are allowed.

The filter is one prefix expression:

- `T` or `F`: Boolean constants.
- `R alias type value`: a comparison, where `value` is `NULL` or a signed 64-bit integer.
- `N expression`: negation.
- `A k expression...`: conjunction of exactly `k` expressions.
- `O k expression...`: disjunction of exactly `k` expressions.

Simplify bottom-up. An `R` with value `NULL` is absent; otherwise it uses `(alias, type)`. Negation preserves absence and negates constants. In each conjunction or disjunction, first delete absent children. In a conjunction, `F` is annihilating and `T` is an identity; an empty conjunction is `T`. In a disjunction, `T` is annihilating and `F` is an identity; an empty disjunction is `F`. If no annihilator applies, references in every remaining nonconstant child are live. Removed references are neither validated nor supplied.

Every live reference must name a declared alias with exactly the referenced type, or the filter is invalid.

A joined index supplies every alias declared for it. A joined set must be dependency-closed: whenever `from` is joined, every index reachable from `from` through one or more dependencies must also be joined. The set must supply every live alias.

Choose a valid joined set with the fewest indexes. Among equally small sets, sort each set by canonical index name and choose the lexicographically smallest list.

Input Specification

The first line contains `D C`. The next `D` lines contain `alias index type`. The next `C` lines contain `from to`. The remaining tokens contain exactly one filter expression.

Constraints: `0 <= D,C <= 200000`; at most 21 distinct canonical indexes; at most 200000 filter nodes; nesting depth at most 512; identifier lengths are 1 to 40; every `k` is nonnegative; the input follows the grammar.

Output Specification

If the schema is conflicting, output `CONFLICT`. Otherwise, if any live reference is invalid, output `INVALID`. Otherwise output the number of joined indexes followed by their canonical names in sorted order.

Output is compared by splitting only on ASCII whitespace bytes `0x09` through `0x0D` and `0x20` and comparing tokens exactly.

Submit one complete Rust program using only the standard library and containing `fn main()`.
